items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Kind of like Duke Ellington. He used to listen to his players noodle, you know. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh yeah?

ctx.x: this piece they were doing that was kind of war between the rock band and the orchestra. So basically I went and played every single part one at a time, of the orchestra, but it was a more in-your-face type of sound because it was a keyboard thing. But it also had a realism to it because if there was five string lines I’d play it with five different sounds and layer it all together. So you could have done it with people, but I was there, and I just did it, and it was a way of making it really tight-sounding. So…
Kind of like Duke Ellington. He used to listen to his players noodle, you know.
